questions.explanation: Correct: eligible means 'you may activate it when you need it.' Activation can require MFA, a justification, and approval, and it lasts for a preconfigured period before it expires. Active means standing privilege with no activation step. The first option describes active, not eligible. The other two are not how PIM works.
options: Nothing — eligible means the role is already active
They must activate it (for example, complete MFA, give a justification, and get approval if required), and the activation lasts only for a limited time
A Global Administrator must delete the assignment and re-create it as active
They must wait 24 hours; eligible assignments activate automatically overnight
questions.question: A user is given the User Administrator role as an eligible assignment. A colleague insists the user can reset passwords immediately. What must happen before they can use it?
questions.source_quote: If users are eligible for a role, then they must activate the role assignment before using the role.

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM role settings let you set maximum activation duration, require MFA on activation, require justification, and require approval by designated approvers, plus notifications. The other options each drop most of those controls or limit PIM to Azure roles only — PIM covers both Entra roles and Azure resources.
options: Only a justification — MFA and approval cannot be required for Entra roles
Maximum activation duration (for example, 8 hours), MFA on activation, justification, and approval by a designated approver
Only approval — duration is always permanent once approved
None — PIM settings apply only to Azure roles, not Entra roles
questions.question: You configure PIM for the User Administrator role. An auditor asks which controls you can require when someone activates it. Which settings are available?
questions.source_quote: Privileged Identity Management provides time-based and approval-based role activation to mitigate the risks of excessive, unnecessary, or misused access permissions on resources that you care about.

questions.explanation: Correct: service principals cannot be eligible — only time-limited active assignments are allowed for them, for Entra roles, Azure roles, and PIM for Groups. The first and third options assume eligibility works for service principals. The fourth is too strong — service principals can hold roles via active assignments.
options: Make the service principal eligible for Global Administrator, so it can activate the role when the runbook starts
Give the service principal a time-limited active assignment only — service principals cannot be eligible for Entra roles, Azure roles, or PIM for Groups
Make the service principal eligible, but only if it is in a role-assignable group
Nothing — service principals cannot hold Entra roles at all
questions.question: You need a service principal used by an automation runbook to have Global Administrator rights for a weekend migration. What can PIM do here?
questions.source_quote: To grant access to a resource, the administrator assigns roles to users, groups, service principals, or managed identities.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM role settings are per role. Configuring User Administrator does not configure Global Administrator — each role has its own settings for maximum duration, MFA, justification, and approval. The first option assumes tenant-wide settings. The third invents a fixed 8-hour rule for Global Administrator. The fourth is false — Global Administrator is a PIM-manageable Entra role.
options: The same settings — PIM settings are tenant-wide and apply to all roles
Nothing yet — role settings are per role, so Global Administrator has its own settings until you configure them
The same settings, but the maximum duration is always 8 hours for Global Administrator regardless
Global Administrator cannot use PIM at all — it must be permanently active
questions.question: You set the User Administrator role to require approval, MFA, justification, and a maximum activation duration of 4 hours. A colleague is eligible for Global Administrator. What applies to them?
questions.source_quote: If users are eligible for a role, then they must activate the role assignment before using the role.

The first option ignores the restriction. The third invents a member/owner split for this restriction — both are blocked.
options: Yes — any security group can be enabled for PIM for Groups
No — dynamic groups and on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups
Yes, but only for the owner role, not the member role
Yes, if you first make the group role-assignable — that fixes both problems
questions.question: You want just-in-time membership of a security group that grants access to Intune and Key Vault. The group is dynamic (membership rule-based) and synced from on-premises. Can you enable PIM for Groups on it?

questions.explanation: Correct: User Administrator is an Entra role — it manages Entra resources (users, groups). It does not grant Azure Resource Manager permissions. Assigning an Azure role on a subscription needs an Azure role at that scope, such as Owner or Role Based Access Control Administrator. PIM for Entra does not grant that. The first option conflates the two RBAC systems. The third invents automatic revocation of the Azure assignment when PIM expires — the Azure assignment is separate. The fourth misreads the duration — 2 hours is within the 8-hour maximum, so duration is not the blocker.
options: It works — User Administrator in Entra includes Azure RBAC assignment rights

It fails — User Administrator is an Entra role for managing Entra resources; assigning Azure roles needs an Azure role such as Owner or Role Based Access Control Administrator on that subscription scope, which PIM for Entra does not grant
It works, but only for 2 hours — after that the Azure assignment is revoked automatically
It fails because PIM activation lasts only 8 hours, and the admin asked for 2 hours
questions.question: A Global Administrator is on holiday. An admin needs User Administrator for 2 hours to reset a contractor's password. The admin is eligible for User Administrator in PIM, with role settings: maximum duration 8 hours, require MFA, require justification, require approval by the Privileged Role Administrator. The admin activates the role, provides a justification, completes MFA, and the approver approves. The admin then tries to assign an Azure Reader role on a subscription to the contractor. What happens?
questions.source_quote: For Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management, only a user who is in the Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator role can manage assignments for other administrators.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM for Groups requires a role-assignable group; once enabled, member and owner assignments can be eligible and activated just-in-time with the usual PIM controls (duration, justification, approval). Dynamic groups and on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups, so those options are backwards. Not every group qualifies — the role-assignable property is the gate.
options: The group must be role-assignable, and membership (and ownership) can then be made eligible for just-in-time activation
The group must be synced from on-premises; cloud-only groups cannot use PIM for Groups
Nothing — any group works, and PIM for Groups converts it automatically
The group must be dynamic; only dynamic groups support PIM for Groups
questions.question: A security group grants access to a sensitive SharePoint site. You want members to hold that membership only when they need it, activating it just-in-time with approval, instead of holding it permanently. What must be true of the group before you can use PIM for Groups on it?
questions.source_quote: Privileged Identity Management provides time-based and approval-based role activation to mitigate the risks of excessive, unnecessary, or misused access permissions on resources that you care about.

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM includes alerts that flag risky configurations, including too many users assigned to a privileged role and assignments that should be eligible rather than permanent. Conditional Access report-only shows policy impact, not role hygiene. Access reviews certify access, they do not convert assignments. The audit log records events, it does not delete assignments.
options: The Entra audit log, which deletes excessive assignments after 30 days
PIM alerts, which flag issues such as excessive privileged role assignments and roles assigned to users who do not need them
Conditional Access report-only mode, which lists Global Administrators
Access reviews, which automatically convert permanent assignments to eligible ones
questions.question: Your tenant has 40 users permanently assigned Global Administrator. The security team wants Privileged Identity Management to surface this as a problem. Which PIM capability highlights risky privileged-role configuration?
questions.source_quote: It's a good idea to check how many users have administrative access, how many of them are Global Administrators, and if there are any invited guests or partners that haven't been removed after being assigned to do an administrative task.
questions.source_title: What are access reviews? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: these are two different settings that sound alike. Maximum activation duration caps a single activation session. 'Expire eligible assignments' removes the eligible assignment itself if it is not used within the configured period — so after 100 days without activation, the eligibility is gone and the user cannot activate until reassigned. The 8-hour cap does not delete eligibility, and the 90-day expiry does not extend an activation to 90 days, and it applies to eligible assignments, not only active ones.
options: The activation lasts 90 days, because the expiry setting overrides the maximum duration
They can activate for 8 hours, because the 90-day expiry only applies to active assignments, not eligible ones
They cannot activate, because the 8-hour maximum has expired; the assignment is gone
They cannot activate: the 90-day expiry removed the eligibility after 100 days without activation, so the assignment must be renewed first — the 8-hour maximum only caps how long one activation lasts
questions.question: A PIM role setting has 'Maximum activation duration: 8 hours' for Global Administrator, and a separate setting 'Expire eligible assignments after 90 days'. An eligible Global Administrator has not activated the role for 100 days, then activates it for a task. What happens?
questions.source_quote: There's no difference in the access given to someone with a permanent versus an eligible role assignment. The only difference is that some people don't need that access all the time.

questions.explanation: Correct: eligible and active assignments grant exactly the same access — the only difference is that an eligible user must activate (and may need MFA, justification, or approval) while an active user holds the privilege continuously. The audit finding is the standing access itself, not a difference in power. The other options invent a permission gap that does not exist.
options: They have identical permissions — eligible only adds an activation step, so the risk is the standing access, not a difference in power
The eligible admin has read-only permissions until activation, then full permissions
The active admin has fewer permissions because PIM restricts standing assignments
The eligible admin cannot be audited, while the active admin's actions are logged
questions.question: Two administrators hold the Security Administrator role: one as a permanent active assignment, one as a permanent eligible assignment. An auditor asks whether the eligible admin is less powerful. What is the correct answer?
questions.source_quote: There's no difference in the access given to someone with a permanent versus an eligible role assignment. The only difference is that some people don't need that access all the time.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM prevents removal of the last active Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator assignments — that guardrail exists precisely so the tenant cannot be left with no administrator. The other options describe actions PIM does not take: it does not auto-promote, does not delete the tenant, and does not require a support ticket to block the removal.
options: PIM automatically promotes the next eligible administrator to active Global Administrator
PIM deletes the tenant after 30 days if no administrator remains
PIM prevents removal of the last active Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator role assignments
PIM allows the removal but requires a Microsoft support ticket first
questions.question: A departing administrator is the last active Global Administrator in the tenant. Another admin tries to remove their assignment in PIM. What happens?
questions.source_quote: Prevent removal of the last active Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator role assignments
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: for Entra roles in PIM, only a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator can manage assignments for other administrators. Security Administrators and Security Readers can view assignments, but cannot manage them. A User Administrator cannot manage PIM assignments for other admins.
options: Any Security Administrator can manage PIM assignments for other administrators
A User Administrator can manage PIM assignments for other administrators
A Security Reader can manage PIM assignments for other administrators
Only a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator can manage assignments for other administrators
questions.question: A Security Administrator wants to make a colleague eligible for the Exchange Administrator role in PIM. Can they do it?
questions.source_quote: For Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management, only a user who is in the Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator role can manage assignments for other administrators.

questions.explanation: Correct: for Azure resource roles in PIM, only a subscription administrator, a resource Owner, or a resource User Access Administrator can manage assignments. Privileged Role Administrators, Security Administrators, and Security Readers do not by default have access to view or manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM — the Entra role does not cross over to Azure resources.
options: Only a subscription administrator, a resource Owner, or a resource User Access Administrator can manage assignments for Azure resource roles in PIM
A Privileged Role Administrator can manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM by default
A Security Reader can manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM by default
Any Global Administrator can manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM by default
questions.question: A Privileged Role Administrator opens PIM for Azure resources and cannot see the subscription's role assignments. A colleague says their Entra role should be enough. Who is right?
questions.source_quote: For Azure resource roles in Privileged Identity Management, only a subscription administrator, a resource Owner, or a resource User Access Administrator can manage assignments for other administrators. questions.explanation: Correct: when a role assignment nears expiration, the user can request an extension; when it has expired, they request a renewal — and both user-initiated actions require approval from a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. Extensions are not automatic, renewals are not self-approved, and the assignment does not silently convert to permanent.
options: The assignment extends itself automatically for the same duration
The user renews it themselves with no approval needed
The user requests an extension before expiry or a renewal after expiry, and either request requires approval from a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator
The assignment converts to a permanent active assignment so the work is not interrupted
questions.question: A consultant's time-bound eligible assignment for the Intune Administrator role expires next week, mid-project. What is the correct way to keep their access, and who must approve it?
questions.source_quote: Both user-initiated actions require an approval from a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator.

questions.explanation: Correct: when approval is required, a notification appears telling the user the request is pending approval, and the member can start using the role only after the request is approved. Approval is not instant, not automatic, and not granted by the requester.
options: The member is notified the request is pending approval and can use the role only after it is approved
The member can use the role immediately while the approval is pending
The approval is granted automatically after one hour if no approver responds
The member approves their own request by confirming the justification a second time
questions.question: An eligible administrator activates the Global Administrator role, which requires approval. What happens between the activation request and the approver's decision?
questions.source_quote: If the role requires approval to activate, a notification appears in the upper right corner of the user's browser informing them the request is pending approval. If an approval isn't required, the member can start using the role.

questions.explanation: Correct: the approver does not require any roles and does not need to be an administrator — approval is a designated workflow step, not a privilege. Microsoft recommends selecting at least two approvers and there are no default approvers. The other options confuse approval with role assignment.
options: The approver must hold the same role they are approving
The approver must be a Global Administrator
The approver is chosen automatically from the tenant's Privileged Role Administrators
The approver needs no role at all and need not be an administrator; Microsoft recommends at least two approvers and there are no default approvers
questions.question: You configure PIM approval for the Security Administrator role and select a business manager with no admin roles as the approver. The manager asks whether they need an admin role to approve. What is the correct answer?
questions.source_quote: Require approval to activate. You can require approval for activation of eligible assignment. The approver doesn't require any roles, nor does the approver need to be an administrator. When using this option, you have to select at least one approver (Microsoft recommends that you select at least two approvers). There are no default approvers.

questions.explanation: Correct: break-glass accounts must have their Global Administrator assignment as permanent active in PIM, not eligible — an eligible break-glass account could be unusable in the exact emergency it exists for. The other options all make the emergency account depend on activation, approval, or expiry.
options: Make the assignment eligible with approval required, so use is audited
Make the assignment eligible with a 90-day expiry, so it is reviewed regularly
Make the Global Administrator assignment active permanent in PIM, not eligible
Make the assignment time-bound active for 8 hours each quarter
questions.question: Your two emergency-access accounts are currently eligible for Global Administrator in PIM. The CISO says this is wrong. What should the assignment be?
questions.source_quote: In Privileged Identity Management, make the Global Administrator role assignment active permanent rather than eligible for your emergency access accounts.

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM for Groups makes group membership and ownership eligible for just-in-time activation — a member activates the membership for a limited time instead of holding it permanently. options: A member activates the group membership just-in-time for a limited period, instead of holding it permanently
The group is converted to a dynamic group with a membership rule
The group is deleted and its members are reassigned individually
Ownership is made permanent and membership is made eligible, but activation is automatic

The fix is a new cloud-only role-assignable group (or moving the membership to one), not a setting change on the synced group.
options: Enable PIM for Groups on the synced group directly — sync source does not matter
Make the synced group role-assignable and PIM for Groups will work
Convert the synced group to dynamic and enable PIM for Groups on it
Create a cloud-only role-assignable group for the just-in-time membership, because on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM keeps you informed by sending email notifications to you and other participants, including links to tasks such as activating, approving, or denying a request, and delegated approvers receive email notifications when a role request is pending. There is no requirement to watch a portal, no SMS-only channel, and no silent activation.
options: The approver must check the PIM portal every hour; PIM sends no notifications
Notifications are sent by SMS only, so the approver needs a registered phone
PIM sends email notifications to participants and approvers, with links to activate, approve, or deny the request
The requester is notified but the approver is not — approvers must poll the audit log
questions.question: An administrator activates a role that requires approval at 2 a.m. How does the designated approver learn about the pending request?
questions.source_quote: PIM keeps you informed by sending you and other participants email notifications. These emails might also include links to relevant tasks, such as activating, approving, or denying a request.

questions.explanation: Correct: an eligible user activates by selecting a specific activation duration within the maximum configured by administrators, and giving the reason for the request. The duration is chosen by the user up to the configured maximum — it is not fixed at the maximum, not chosen by the approver, and not unlimited.
options: The user selects an activation duration within the configured maximum and provides the reason for the request
The user always receives the maximum duration, with no choice
The approver chooses the duration after approving, and the user cannot select it
The activation lasts until the user signs out, regardless of the configured maximum
questions.question: A role's maximum activation duration is 8 hours. An eligible administrator needs the role for 2 hours. What do they do at activation time?
questions.source_quote: To activate the role, users select specific activation duration within the maximum (configured by administrators), and the reason for the activation request.

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM for Azure resources uses the same eligible/active model — make the role eligible at the resource-group scope with justification and approval, and the user activates it just-in-time. A permanent active assignment defeats PIM. A tenant-wide assignment is the wrong scope. And an Entra role cannot grant Azure permissions.
options: Give them Contributor permanently as an active assignment on the subscription
Give them Contributor permanently, but only at the resource-group scope
Give them the Entra User Administrator role, which includes Azure Contributor rights
Make Contributor an eligible assignment at the resource-group scope, with activation requiring justification and approval

questions.source_quote: Privileged Identity Management provides time-based and approval-based role activation to mitigate the risks of excessive, unnecessary, or misused access permissions on resources that you care about.

A permanent eligible assignment has no end date, a time-bound active assignment grants standing access during the window, and eligibility does not auto-extend.
options: A time-bound eligible assignment — the member can only activate within the start and end dates
A permanent eligible assignment — the member can activate at any time forever
A time-bound active assignment — the member holds the role continuously during the window with no activation step
A permanent active assignment with a calendar reminder to remove it

options: It automatically deletes any assignment older than 90 days
It replaces Conditional Access for privileged users
It provides just-in-time privileged access, time-bound assignments, approval and MFA on activation, justification, notifications, access reviews, and a downloadable audit history
It grants P2 licences to every user who activates a role

questions.explanation: Correct: the assignment includes the members, the scope limiting the role to a particular set of resources, the type (eligible or active), and the duration. Scope is a first-class part of the assignment — it is not tenant-wide by default, not chosen by the member, and not the same as the approval workflow.
options: The assignment has no scope — every PIM role applies tenant-wide
The scope is chosen by the member at activation time

The assignment includes the members, the scope limiting the role to a particular set of resources, the type, and the duration

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM's purpose is to minimise the number of people with access to secure resources, because that reduces the chance of a malicious actor getting access and of an authorised user inadvertently impacting a sensitive resource — while still letting users carry out privileged operations just-in-time. It is not about headcount reduction, cost, or removing the need for admins.
options: To minimise the number of people with standing access to secure resources, reducing the chance of a malicious actor getting access or an authorised user inadvertently impacting a sensitive resource
To reduce the number of administrators the organisation employs
To eliminate the need for Conditional Access policies for privileged users
To make all administrative access permanent so audits are simpler
questions.question: A director asks why the organisation should bother with PIM at all, when the current admins 'have always had permanent access and nothing bad happened'. What is PIM's stated purpose?
questions.source_quote: Organizations want to minimize the number of people who have access to secure information or resources, because that reduces the chance of a malicious actor getting access, an authorized user inadvertently impacting a sensitive resource.

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM covers Microsoft Entra roles, Azure resource roles, and PIM for Groups — the three manage options in the PIM blade. options: Microsoft Entra roles and SharePoint site permissions only
Azure resource roles and on-premises Active Directory groups only
Microsoft Entra roles, Azure resource roles, and PIM for Groups
Third-party SaaS application roles only
questions.question: Your team is scoping a PIM rollout. Which three things can PIM actually manage?
questions.source_quote: Once you set up Privileged Identity Management, you'll see Tasks, Manage, and Activity options in the left navigation menu. As an administrator, you can choose between options such as managing Microsoft Entra roles, managing Azure resource roles, or PIM for Groups.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: activation can require an MFA check, a business justification, or approval from designated approvers — and the role settings can require all three at once. An MFA check, a business justification, and/or approval from designated approvers, as configured in the role settings
questions.question: An eligible administrator is about to activate the Privileged Role Administrator role. The role settings require MFA, justification, and approval. What must the activation include?

options: The member can start using the role immediately after activating it

questions.question: An eligible administrator activates the Helpdesk Administrator role, which has no approval requirement. When can they start using it?

options: It works — PIM for Groups is included in P1

options: Yes — PIM assignments can be made to managed identities as well as users, groups, and service principals

questions.source_quote: To grant access to a resource, the administrator assigns roles to users, groups, service principals, or managed identities.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: once activated, the user can use the role for a preconfigured period before they need to activate again — the activation expires on its own and the user must re-activate. It does not stay active until sign-out, does not require re-approval to expire, and does not convert to permanent.
options: The role stays active until the user signs out
The role stays active until an approver revokes it
The activation expires after the preconfigured period and the user must activate again to continue
The role converts to a permanent active assignment after the first activation
questions.question: An administrator activates the User Administrator role for 4 hours, finishes the task in 1 hour, and leaves the role alone. What happens after 4 hours?
questions.source_quote: Once activated, the user can use the role for a preconfigured period of time before they need to activate again.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: the audit history is a PIM feature — you can download the audit history for internal or external audit, and every activation is recorded. PIM does not hide activations, does not only log denials, and does not require a separate SIEM to have a record.
options: Only denied activations are logged; approved ones are not recorded
Activations are logged only if the tenant has Microsoft Sentinel connected
The audit history is available only to Microsoft support on request
Every activation is recorded and the audit history can be downloaded for internal or external audit
questions.question: An auditor asks for proof of every Global Administrator activation in the last 90 days, including who approved each one. Where does that evidence come from in PIM?
questions.source_quote: Download audit history for internal or external audit
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: a Privileged Role Administrator can enable approval for specific roles, specify approver users or groups, and view request and approval history for all privileged roles. They cannot approve their own activation, cannot delete the tenant, and cannot bypass MFA on activation.
options: Enable approval for specific roles, specify approver users or groups, and view request and approval history for all privileged roles
Approve their own role activation without another approver
Delete the tenant's PIM configuration without confirmation
Bypass the MFA requirement on activation for themselves
questions.question: What can a Privileged Role Administrator do in PIM that an ordinary eligible administrator cannot?
questions.source_quote: Enable approval for specific roles. Specify approver users or groups to approve requests. View request and approval history for all privileged roles.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: an approver can view pending approvals, approve or reject requests for role elevation (single and bulk), and provide justification for the approval or rejection. Approvers cannot grant the role permanently, cannot change the role settings, and cannot activate the role for the requester.
options: The approver can grant the role permanently instead of time-limited
The approver can change the role's maximum activation duration
The approver can view pending approvals, approve or reject requests (single and bulk), and provide justification for the decision
The approver can activate the role on the requester's behalf
questions.question: A designated approver receives a PIM activation request for the Security Administrator role. What can they do with it?
questions.source_quote: View pending approvals (requests). Approve or reject requests for role elevation (single and bulk). Provide justification for my approval or rejection.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: just-in-time access is the model where users receive temporary permissions to perform privileged tasks, which prevents malicious or unauthorised users from gaining access after the permissions expire — access is granted only when needed. It is not permanent access with logging, not a synonym for approval, and not limited to groups.
options: Permanent access that is logged more carefully
Access granted only after two approvers sign off, with no expiry
Access that is always active but hidden from the directory
Temporary permissions granted only when needed, expiring automatically so they cannot be used afterwards
questions.question: A board member asks what 'just-in-time access' actually means in PIM, in one sentence. Which definition is correct?
questions.source_quote: A model in which users receive temporary permissions to perform privileged tasks, which prevents malicious or unauthorized users from gaining access after the permissions expire. Access is granted only when users need it.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: least privilege means every user is provided with only the minimum privileges needed to accomplish the tasks they are authorised to perform, minimising the number of Global Administrators and using specific roles instead. It is not about giving everyone the same role, not about time limits alone, and not about removing all admin roles.
options: Every user gets only the minimum privileges needed for the tasks they are authorised to perform, minimising Global Administrators in favour of specific roles
Every administrator gets Global Administrator so no task is ever blocked
Least privilege means access expires after 8 hours regardless of the task
Least privilege means no user may hold more than one role at a time
questions.question: A manager proposes giving every IT staff member Global Administrator 'to keep things simple'. Which principle does PIM's least-privilege model contradict, and what does it require instead?
questions.source_quote: A recommended security practice in which every user is provided with only the minimum privileges needed to accomplish the tasks they're authorized to perform. This practice minimizes the number of Global Administrators and instead uses specific administrator roles for certain scenarios.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: an eligible role user can request activation of a role that requires approval, view the status of the request, and complete the task if activation was approved. They cannot approve their own request, cannot change the role settings, and cannot see other users' pending requests.
options: Approve their own activation request
Change the role's activation settings
Request activation of a role that requires approval, view the status of the request, and complete the task if activation was approved
View and approve other users' activation requests
questions.question: What can an eligible role user do in PIM for themselves?
questions.source_quote: Request activation of a role that requires approval. View the status of your request to activate. Complete your task in Microsoft Entra ID if activation was approved.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: the owner activates the owner assignment and the member activates the member assignment — PIM for Groups covers both membership and ownership as eligible assignments. Ownership is not automatically permanent, not shared with all members, and not excluded from PIM for Groups.
options: Only members can be eligible; owners are always permanent
Owners cannot activate anything — only members can
Ownership is inherited automatically by every member who activates
Both member and owner assignments can be eligible and activated just-in-time
questions.question: A role-assignable group has eligible members and an eligible owner. The owner needs to approve a membership change that only owners can make. What must the owner do first?
questions.source_quote: Privileged Identity Management provides time-based and approval-based role activation to mitigate the risks of excessive, unnecessary, or misused access permissions on resources that you care about.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: after the request is approved, the member can start using the role — approval is the gate, and the delegated approver's decision is what unlocks it. The member does not wait for a second approval, does not need to re-activate, and the approval does not expire instantly.
options: After the request is approved, the member can start using the role
The member must activate a second time after approval before the role works
The member must wait for a second approver even when only one is configured
The approval expires immediately, so the member must request again within one minute
questions.question: A delegated approver approves a pending request for the Contributor role on a resource group. What happens next for the requester?
questions.source_quote: After the request is approved, the member can start using the role.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM sends notifications when privileged roles are activated, and the audit history records every activation — the Security team can review who activated what and when, and whether approval and MFA were satisfied. There is no silent activation path in PIM, and the admin cannot suppress the audit trail.
options: Nothing is recorded — PIM activations are private to the user
Only the approver is notified, and no record is kept
PIM sends notifications when privileged roles are activated and records every activation in the audit history
The activation is recorded only if the admin also files a change ticket
questions.question: A Global Administrator activates their role at 3 a.m. without telling anyone. How does the Security team find out?
questions.source_quote: Get notifications when privileged roles are activated. Download audit history for internal or external audit.
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: use justification to understand why users activate — justification is a PIM feature that records the business reason for each activation, and it can be required by the role settings. It is not a free-text note that is discarded, not a replacement for approval, and not visible only to the user.
options: Justification is optional decoration that PIM discards after activation
Justification replaces approval — a good reason means no approver is needed
Justification is visible only to the user who entered it
Justification records the business reason for the activation and can be required by the role settings, so reviewers can understand why the role was used
questions.question: An auditor reviewing PIM activations asks why every activation carries a justification field. What is its purpose?
questions.source_quote: Use justification to understand why users activate
questions.source_title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: PIM can manage role assignments for a group — a group can be made eligible for a role, and members activate the role through the group — which is how you give a whole on-call team just-in-time access without assigning each person individually. The group itself is not the approver, the role is not automatically active for all members, and the group does not need to be deleted.
options: Assign the role to the group as eligible in PIM, so members of the group activate the role just-in-time when on call
Assign the role permanently to every member of the group individually
Make the group the approver for its own role activations
Delete the group and assign the role to a service principal instead
questions.question: An on-call team of six engineers shares a security group. They need the Security Reader role just-in-time during incidents, without six separate permanent assignments. How can PIM handle this?
questions.source_quote: To grant access to a resource, the administrator assigns roles to users, groups, service principals, or managed identities.
